_note: Constants the Puzzle Pirates wiki does not publish are invented here and nowhere else, so invented numbers stay visibly separate from sourced ones and tuning stays a data change. Every key carries an entry in _sources saying where its value came from; a key with no entry is a bug.

_sources.bilging.boardWidth: invented; the wiki never states the grid dimensions
_sources.bilging.boardHeight: invented; the wiki only requires at least 3 water rows and at least 3 dry top rows, so the height must be at least 6
_sources.bilging.colourCountByStarLevel: invented, anchored on the published 7 colours at star level 7
_sources.bilging.maxStarLevel: the star level the wiki anchors on: 7 colours, and every critter unlocked, the jellyfish last at 6
_sources.bilging.startingStarLevel: scope decision; an offline pirate starts with no standing to draw a difficulty from
_sources.bilging.ticksPerStarStep: invented; one star level per minute of play at 60 ticks per second
_sources.bilging.comboMultiplierByLineCount: published for 1, 2 and 3 lines; index 4 is the low end of the published range at least 4, maybe 5; index 5 is invented
_sources.bilging.comboScalePerMilleByStarLevel: invented; the wiki publishes the combo table at 7-star level and only says the multipliers are lower below it, so index 7 is 1000 to keep the published table exact
_sources.bilging.vegasMultiplier: the low end of the published range at least 5, maybe 6-7
_sources.bilging.chainPointsPerCell: published; a chain is worth no more than 1 point per block cleared
_sources.bilging.pufferSpawnPerMille: invented; the wiki never states how often a critter appears, and the puffer is the commonest of the three
_sources.bilging.crabSpawnPerMille: invented; rarer than the puffer because a crab denies its square until it climbs out
_sources.bilging.jellySpawnPerMille: invented; the rarest of the three, since one jelly clears a whole colour
_sources.bilging.crabPointsAtFullWater: invented against the published anchor that two crabs cleared at full water score between a bingo of 27 and a sea donkey of 48; 9 puts two crabs at 36
_sources.bilging.pufferPointsPerCell: published in effect; the wiki calls the puffer score-negative, so the detonation itself pays nothing and only the chain it triggers scores
_sources.bilging.jellyPointsPerCell: invented; a jelly sweep is worth no more per cell than a chain
_sources.bilging.aboveWaterFallTicksPerCell: invented; the wiki says only that pieces fall more slowly below the water line, never how much
_sources.bilging.belowWaterFallTicksPerCell: invented; twice the dry rate, the smallest ratio that reads as slower
_sources.bilging.inflowPerMillePerThousandTicks: invented; the bilge-to-performance coupling rate is nowhere on the wiki. An ignored board floods from empty to full in about 119 seconds
_sources.bilging.pumpPerMillePerThousandTicks: invented; the board drains at any efficiency above 467 per mille and empties from full in about 104 seconds at 100 per cent efficiency
_sources.bilging.ratingBandsPerMille: invented; the lower bound of poor, fine, good, excellent and incredible, honouring the published fine at about 100 per cent and sparkly at 4 points per move
_sources.ship.bilgeInflowPerMillePerThousandTicks: invented; an unmanned ship at sea floods unchecked, and 28 fills a hull from empty to full in 10 minutes, inside the published 15 to 30 minute unmanned reset window, so an abandoned ship is in trouble before the reset would have saved it
_sources.ship.damageBilgeCoefficientPerMille: invented; only the direction of the damage-to-bilge coupling is published, and 1000 doubles the intake at full damage, the smallest coupling a player can feel while the loop stays bounded
_sources.ship.carpentryBilgeSlowingPerMille: invented; good carpentry slows the rate at which bilge enters, a path independent of damage, and 300 cuts the base intake by 30 per cent at perfect carpentry, visible but far short of replacing the bilger
_sources.ship.wearDamagePerMillePerThousandTicks: invented; wear and tear is explicitly unquantified, and 2 fills a sloop from empty to full in about 2 hours of wholly uncrewed sailing, slow enough to read as wear and fast enough that an unmanned voyage is not free
_sources.ship.carpentryRepairPerMillePerThousandT: invented; carpenters must make more shots than the published ceiling necessary without stalling a competent attacker, and 33 offsets about a third of the fire a sloop takes at two small hits per turn
_sources.ship.bilgePumpPerMillePerThousandTicksAt: invented; reuses the tuned bilging pump rate, which against a ship inflow of 28 drains at any output above about 93 per mille, a gentler bar than the puzzle board because a hull floods over 10 minutes rather than 2
_sources.ship.bilgeSpeedCapPerMille: invented; bilge caps achievable speed rather than subtracting from it, and 800 caps a full bilge at 20 per cent of the class maximum, crawling but never stopped, consistent with the published floor of 0.2 leagues per minute
_sources.ship.navigationBonusMaxPerMille: invented; duty navigation multiplies the sailors' effectiveness, and 500 adds 50 per cent at perfect navigation, a bonus that matters without making the sailors irrelevant
_sources.ship.warGalleonRamDamageSmallMicro: invented; the war galleon ram damage cell is blank and verify-tagged on both source pages, so it takes the war brig value of two small-cannonball equivalents, the class whose sinking damage it already shares
_sources.ship.rumPerPiratePerThousandTicks: invented; the rum consumption rate is nowhere on the wiki, and 1 is the slowest rate that still lets a ship run dry and so gate the rum sickness handicap in the melee
_sources.battle.movementTokenMilliPerThousandTick: invented; a turn is 35 seconds or 2100 ticks at 60 ticks per second, so 1900 funds a sloop's published allowance of 4 movement tokens per turn at perfect sailing and rigging output and no more, and leaves larger classes a surplus their 3 of 4 budget then loses to expiry
_sources.battle.bilgeTokenThrottlePerMille: invented; only the direction of the bilge-to-token coupling is published, and 700 drops generation to 30 per cent at full bilge, clearly felt without reaching zero, which would deadlock a battle whose only other exit is disengage
_sources.battle.cannonLoadMilliPerThousandTicksAt: invented; half the movement rate, so perfect gunnery loads about 2 cannons per 35 second turn against a sloop's 4 loaded and 8 legal shots, which makes gunnery the binding constraint on sustained fire
_sources.npc.crewDutyOutputPerMille: invented, anchored on the published crew requirement table assuming low fine swabbie performance; 900 is the lower bound of fine in bilging.ratingBandsPerMille, so the published swabbie counts come out right by construction
_sources.npc.brigandCrewDutyOutputPerMille: invented; the same value as the player crew so the first brigand is a mirror and difficulty comes from AI quality and ship class rather than a hidden output advantage, kept separate so difficulty tuning has its own lever
_sources.brigand.planLookaheadPhases: invented; one full turn, because a plan the game commits a whole turn at a time cannot be scored on less, and more would speculate about tokens that do not exist yet
_sources.brigand.weightCloseDistance: invented; the baseline plan weight per tile of range closed, positive so brigands close and the battle resolves
_sources.brigand.weightBroadsideExposure: invented; three times the closing weight, so the AI prefers a firing line to a straight charge, the behaviour a human reads as competence
_sources.brigand.weightIncomingBroadside: invented; slightly below its own offence weight, so it trades shots rather than turtling
_sources.brigand.weightRockCollision: invented; dominates every positive weight, because a move into a rock or the board edge is pure loss
_sources.brigand.geniusChancePerMille: invented; the only published characterisation is that bots have random spurts of genius, and 100 makes about one turn in ten evaluate with full lookahead and no noise
_sources.brigand.blunderNoisePerMille: invented; a deterministic scorer plays the same battle every time and stops feeling like an opponent, and 30 is three tiles of weightCloseDistance, enough that two brigands on the same board diverge, while still below the weight of a broadside worth taking and far below the penalty for a rock worth avoiding
_sources.brigand.disengageAtDamagePerMille: invented; the brigand must be able to run or disengaging is a player-only mechanic, and 700 still leaves the player a real chance to finish it first
_sources.booty.brigandPoeBase: invented; half of captured PoE goes to the chest and half splits instantly, and 800 over a seven-pirate sloop crew is a payout a player notices per battle without trivialising a voyage
_sources.booty.brigandPoePerMightMilli: invented; payouts are published as scaling with might, crew size and opponent rank, and 1000 makes that scaling linear in the might scalar, the simplest defensible curve
_sources.booty.brigandPoeVariancePerMille: invented; a spread of plus or minus 25 per cent, wide enough that two identical battles pay differently and narrow enough not to swamp the might scaling
_sources.booty.brigandCargoUnitsBase: invented; deliberately small against a sloop hold of 13500 kilograms so the overflow policy is rarely exercised
_sources.booty.chartDropChancePerMille: invented; brigand vessels may additionally drop a new chart, and 200 makes charts a reliable pillage reward without flooding the navigation table
_sources.booty.overflowPolicy: invented; the wiki never describes what happens when a capture exceeds the remaining hold capacity, and truncate, which takes what fits in descending unit value and discards the rest, is the only policy that cannot corrupt the hold invariant; refuse and spill-to-sea are the alternatives worth exposing
_sources.battle.tallRockCount: invented; the wiki publishes the tile kinds but never how a sea battle board is laid out, and 6 tall rocks on 576 tiles give the board enough cover to break a line of fire without turning it into a maze
_sources.battle.smallRockCount: invented; small rocks block movement but not fire, so they outnumber tall rocks to make ramming hazards commoner than firing cover
_sources.battle.windTileCount: invented; wind is published as a tile that pushes a resting ship one square to leeward, and 4 tiles keep it an occasional surprise rather than a current that dominates navigation
_sources.battle.startingSeparationTiles: invented; the opening formation of a sea battle is nowhere on the wiki, and 17 of the 24 rows leave both ships about four turns of closing before the first broadside
_sources.battle.startingCannonballs: scope decision; the port economy that stocks a magazine arrives in slice 4, and 40 balls is ten reloads of a sloop four-cannon battery, enough that running dry is a long battle rather than the normal case
_sources.battle.startingRum: scope decision; rum is bought in port, which does not exist yet, and 20 units keep a sloop crew off the rum sickness handicap for a single pillage
